core_obligations: Build a surjection from a symmetric algebra (proof lines 3607-3616): take a finitely presented module F with a surjection onto A and use the algebra structure to obtain a surjection from the symmetric algebra on F onto A, whose kernel is denoted J.

Present the kernel and define the approximants (proof lines 3616-3626): write J as a filtered colimit of finite type submodules E_i, and let A_i be the quotient of the symmetric algebra by the ideal generated by E_i; each A_i is a finitely presented algebra, the transition maps are surjections and the colimit is A.

Make the approximants finite (proof lines 3626-3636): cover X by finitely many affine opens, choose generators of F over each and monic polynomials satisfied by their images in A over that affine open; since A is the colimit of the A_i, those polynomial relations hold in A_i over the affine open for all sufficiently large i, so for such i the algebras A_i are finite, which completes the proof.
proof_roadmap: Present the algebra as a quotient of the symmetric algebra on a finitely presented module.
Approximate the kernel by finite type submodules to get finitely presented approximants with surjective transition maps.
Use monic relations over a finite affine cover to make the approximants finite for large index.
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that a finite quasi-coherent algebra on a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme is a directed colimit of finite and finitely presented quasi-coherent algebras with surjective transition maps (statement lines 3597-3605). The proof (proof lines 3607-3638) presents the algebra as a quotient of the symmetric algebra on a finitely presented module, approximates the kernel by finite type submodules to obtain finitely presented approximants, and uses monic relations over a finite affine cover to make them finite.
